messages:
kyle: Quick run — generated a surface/heatmap comparing SSE vs WebSocket across regions (us-east, eu-west) and GPU families (A10G, A100Q). High-level: SSE shows lower p50 but has worse p99 under bursty traffic. Charts attached :chart_with_upwards_trend:

bench-bot: started bench job 1734567890 at 2024-11-05T14:02:10Z — agents: wrk/vegeta, 512B payload, 8 concurrency

maggie: nice. what was the payload distribution and batch config? was batching on at the frontend?

kyle: payload ~ 512B median, 2KB 95p. batching: non-stream endpoints used dynamic batching window=5ms, streaming (SSE/WS) had batching disabled (single-token streaming). snippet:
```
# vegeta profile (simplified)
rate=200
duration=300s
headers: Authorization, Content-Type
body: prompt.json
```

raj: raw numbers from us-east / A100Q (cold starts included):
- SSE: p50=22ms, p95=120ms, p99=480ms, throughput=220 req/s sustained (tail spikes at bursts)
- WebSocket: p50=28ms, p95=95ms, p99=150ms, throughput=190 req/s
Notes: SSE better p50/throughput due to continuous chunking, but p99 suffers from head-of-line KV-cache misses and context-switch churn under bursts.

sarah: we ran these on bf16 for correctness. int8 quant gave ~2.5x throughput but caused eval regressions (summ-eval ROUGE drop ~0.08). also: enabling fused attention kernel on A100Q improved SSE p50 by ~10% in repeat runs.

kyle: uploaded heatmap + 3D surface plot to the bench dashboard: https://bench.redwood.example/1734567890 — surface shows clear ridge where SSE p99 spikes when concurrency > 300 and model kv-cache miss rate > 5%.

maggie: for Dedicated sizing — rough rule from these runs: 1x A100Q handles ~220 sustained SSE req/s with p50~25ms; i'd recommend 3x A100Q per 1k concurrent streaming clients to keep p99 < 250ms and headroom for bursts.

raj: +1. I'll run a follow-up split: warm vs cold cache, and kernel selection toggles (fused vs reference) tomorrow. plan: include a small experiment enabling small batching for SSE (2-3ms window) to see p99 effect.

bench-bot: results and raw traces uploaded -> s3://redwood-bench/results/1734567890 (includes token-level traces, kernel tags) :white_check_mark:

sarah: action item: capture token-latency traces + kernel-selection labels in logs so we can correlate p99 spikes to kernel fallbacks. also tag quantization config in metadata.

kyle: great threads. i'll collate into a one-pager for eng-ml benchboard and ping @eng-infra about rollout policy changes (canary to WS fallback when SSE p99 > 300ms). thanks all :tada:
